item.title: Police Officer Says He Recognized AKA Murder Suspect In Airport Video
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: AKA's murder trial heard a police officer explain why he identified a defendant in airport footage the defense had challenged.
item.content:encoded:
AKA‘s murder trial has a new answer to a disputed question: a police officer says he recognized the defendant shown following the South African rapper at the airport.

The officer, who collects CCTV evidence, told the Durban High Court that the man was Mziwethemba Gwabeni, one of the seven accused, according to an October 22 report from SABC News.

He said he knew Gwabeni from past encounters in police cells, other footage and news reports. The officer was convinced Gwabeni was the man seen behind AKA and his group at King Shaka International Airport.

His account also explained how police reached that view. The case’s investigating officer first pointed to someone in the video. The CCTV officer then took a closer look and agreed.

“We then came to the conclusion that it was the same person,” he told the court.

All seven men deny the charges. The state still has to prove its case against each of them. No verdict has been reached.

The case includes murder, conspiracy, attempted murder and gun charges.

The distinction matters because the earlier airport witness did not identify Gwabeni. When the state showed the footage on October 19, it did not ask the airport’s analyst to identify the man seen near AKA.

Gwabeni’s lawyer, William Nicholson, argued that the person could not be identified and that the analyst lacked the ability to do so.

The court saw AKA stop at a car-rental counter. A man stood near the entrance, then appeared to follow the rapper toward the parking lot. That sequence put the identity dispute at the heart of the airport evidence.

The analyst also described a limit on the airport’s system: it could not export the footage to other devices. He could produce still images, which he had supplied to the state.

Police had already alleged at a bail hearing that Gwabeni followed AKA. The latest account adds a trial witness’s stated basis for identifying him, rather than leaving that claim with the earlier bail case.

AKA and Tebello “Tibz” Motsoane were killed in Durban on February 10, 2023. All seven accused have pleaded not guilty.

item.title: RAYE Beats Dave & Paul McCartney To Mercury Prize
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: RAYE won the 2026 Mercury Prize for her second album, telling the Newcastle crowd she hoped her music could help listeners.
item.content:encoded:
RAYE won the 2026 Mercury Prize for This Music May Contain Hope on October 22, beating a field that included Dave, Olivia Dean and Paul McCartney. The British singer collected the honor in Newcastle for her second studio album.

It was her first Mercury win after My 21st Century Blues made the 2023 shortlist but lost to Ezra Collective.

In her speech, RAYE contrasted the award’s focus on albums with the pressure to keep chasing singles. She said that recognition meant a great deal to her, even as she had largely made peace with her past.

She also spoke about what she hoped listeners would take from the record. “Music is medicine, so I just hope as well that message comes across to anyone who needs it,” RAYE said, according to Reuters.

An earlier Abbey Road session offered another setting for that music. RAYE’s official October 8 upload of “I Will Overcome.” credited the London Symphony Orchestra, conductor Tom Richards and the Flames Collective choir.

The judges’ announcement explained why her record stood out. They praised its four-part design and its movement through soul, R&B, jazz and classical music.

For the panel, those choices served one woman’s story of love and daily life rather than trapping her in one sound. Their statement also defended the album’s role in the streaming era, describing the format as a way for artists to put a complete creative statement into the world.

The prize itself rewards a full album, with an independent panel choosing from British and Irish acts across genres. Judges make their final choice on the night of the ceremony.

This year’s panel included musicians Jamie Cullum and MistaJam, with music executive Jeff Smith chairing.

The winner received a 25,000-pound prize. RAYE followed Sam Fender, who won last year with People Watching.

For the winning performance, the album returned to center stage.

Host Lauren Laverne led the ceremony at Utilita Arena, and broadcaster Sian Eleri presented RAYE with the trophy on the judges’ behalf. RAYE then performed “I Hate The Way I Look Today.” and received a standing ovation, according to the organizers.

item.title: Cesar Pina Pleads Guilty To Fraud, Money Laundering & Bribery
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Cesar Pina admitted fraud, money laundering and bribery in federal court. His sentencing is scheduled for March 10, 2027.
item.content:encoded:
Cesar Pina has pleaded guilty to a multimillion-dollar real estate fraud scheme that took investors’ money while he laundered drug proceeds and paid bribes to a New Jersey official.

The 48-year-old Franklin Lakes resident entered his plea October 22 before U.S. District Judge Madeline Cox Arleo in Newark. His plea covered wire fraud, money laundering conspiracy and two bribery offenses, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office.

Pina, known online as “Flipping NJ,” often promised returns of at least 30 percent within four to five months. Instead, prosecutors said, he used fresh investments to pay earlier investors and cover personal and unrelated business costs.

The 19-page charging document details how Pina raised money for homes he already owned without telling investors about existing mortgages or other people backing the same property.

One example involved a Paterson property on Manchester Avenue that Pina bought for about $140,000 in 2019. He continued seeking investments in that home through April 2023, the filing says.

An August 2022 contract promised one investor a $30,000 return on a $100,000 stake within five months. That investor sent Pina roughly $600,000 for three properties, including the Manchester Avenue home. Across the scheme, the filing says victims still lacked “most or all of their promised principal and interest.”

Prosecutors also traced investor funds to luxury clothes, vacations, vehicles and beauty supplies. The filing describes millions in losses across dozens of victims.

The case reached beyond those property deals. Pina also admitted conspiring to launder money for people he knew were involved in drug trafficking.

The bribery scheme centered on his “Old School 5” project in Paterson. Pina wanted to turn a former school into a 60-unit apartment complex. The filing describes about $50,000 in cash and check payments to an unnamed official, plus property listings that let the official earn commissions. The two bribery counts involve a federally funded program and the Travel Act.

The guilty plea follows three years of criminal proceedings. Authorities arrested Pina in October 2023 on a wire fraud complaint. He secured his release on a $1 million bond.

AllHipHop reported tighter bail terms in March 2024. Those terms required approval from Pretrial Services before Pina could create or use social media accounts. They also barred him from opening new bank accounts or credit lines without permission.

Magistrate Judge Edward S. Kiel also ordered him to remove guns and ammunition from his residence and surrender firearm permits. His lawyer told the court that Pina had deactivated his social media accounts.

By April 2024, plea talks were underway. Judge Leda Dunn Wettre granted more time for both sides to negotiate, according to court records AllHipHop obtained then.

That August, Pina asked the court to let him drive for Uber and Lyft. His attorney said he had received tentative approval to start work and sought broader travel permission across New Jersey, New York, Connecticut and Pennsylvania.

The proposed change excluded trips to airports. His lawyer wrote that Pretrial Services accepted the proposal with that exception, while prosecutors had not yet provided a position.

The case grew in 2025. AllHipHop covered a six-count indictment that July that added money laundering and bribery allegations to the fraud case. The indictment included two wire fraud counts, a laundering conspiracy count, two money laundering counts and a bribery count.

The fraud and laundering conspiracy counts each carry up to 20 years in prison. The bribery counts carry maximums of 10 and five years. Judge Arleo is scheduled to sentence Pina March 10, 2027.

item.title: Hei$enberg Releases Highly Anticipated Single “Big Papi”
item.dc:creator: Staff Writer
item.description: Texas artist Hei$enberg brings bold bars and box Chevy energy to “Big Papi,” a hard-hitting anthem about success, self-assurance, and moving in your own lane.
item.content:encoded:
“Big Papi” is a hard-hitting braggadocio rap track from Texas-based artist Hei$enberg, delivering bold confidence, unapologetic energy, and a sound made for riding out. With its box Chevy vibe and larger-than-life attitude, the record celebrates success, self-assurance, and standing tall in your own lane. Big Papi is a statement track for those who move with confidence and let their presence speak for itself. Make sure you check out “Big Papi” out now on all platforms and follow Hei$enberg on social media for his latest releases.

Connect:

http://www.instagram.com/heisenberg409

item.title: Ken Carson Takes Halloween To Roblox With More Than A Concert
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Ken Carson announced Roblox concerts for Halloween weekend, with game tie-ins starting before his virtual shows.
item.content:encoded:
Ken Carson is bringing his Halloween show to Roblox, with plans that extend beyond a single virtual stage and into three of the platform’s games.

The Atlanta rapper’s concerts in “The Block” are set for October 30 and October 31 at 4 P.M. Pacific. That is 7 P.M. Eastern. The performances are still ahead, with the first game tie-ins arriving before the concert dates.

“The Mimic” and “Blade Ball” will get Carson integrations on October 26. “Fisch” will follow on October 31. The game events start four days before his first show, giving fans a way into the takeover before the music begins.

The new announcement also pointed to his “xperimenting Tour” and his recent headline set at ComplexCon Los Angeles.

This year’s music included xperiment and cartunez, following 2025’s More Chaos. The July album rollout also included short films directed by Joy Divizn. His team is now building the Halloween event around the live side of that run.

His team pitched the event as a way to bring his stage show’s look and feel into a shared virtual space.

Carson already took that live show to festival crowds this year. At Rolling Loud Orlando in May, he brought out Young Thug and Lil Tecca during his closing-night set. The festival also streamed on Twitch, Prime Video and the Amazon Music app.

Roblox’s music events predate Carson’s announcement.

In December 2025, Universal Music Group announced a partnership with the platform that included artist experiences and plans for digital and physical merchandise sales through Shopify.

Earlier UMG projects on Roblox included Beat Galaxy, a music-discovery space, and Boombox, which brought licensed music into games through Styngr.

The UMG deal also offered artists help with creating and running their events, plus access to new Roblox tools and features still in testing.

Carson’s announcement didn’t detail in-game merchandise or explain how each game tie-in would work. Its first scheduled stop is “The Mimic” and “Blade Ball” on October 26, followed by the two Halloween-weekend concerts.

item.title: Doja Cat Brings Out Rico Nasty For A “Tia Tamera” Birthday Reunion
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Doja Cat brought Rico Nasty out for "Tia Tamera" at her hometown birthday show, with the reunion set to air October 29.
item.content:encoded:
Doja Cat had a familiar partner for her hometown birthday show: Rico Nasty, who joined her to perform “Tia Tamera” at the Kia Forum on Thursday night.

Rico made a surprise appearance during the October 22 stop on Doja’s “Tour Ma Vie World Tour” in Inglewood, California. The two returned to a song they released together in 2019.

Amazon Music confirmed the guest spot in a statement shared with AllHipHop on Friday and posted a preview on its official YouTube account.

Doja had singled out the hometown date when Amazon announced the show in September.

“I’m playing The Forum the day after my birthday and I’m spending it onstage doing what I love most. That’s already special,” she said.

The choice of “Tia Tamera” took the show back to her debut album’s run. The song arrived in February 2019 ahead of the deluxe edition of Amala, with Rico as its guest. It followed “Mooo!,” the song and video that had brought Doja a wave of online attention the year before.

The track’s video paired the rappers in a bright, 1990s-inspired world. Director Roxana Baldovin drew on “Sister, Sister” and Nickelodeon’s “Double Dare,” giving their playful collaboration a game-show setting.

Rico later said the track worked because she hadn’t overthought it. In a 2022 Glamour interview, she recalled matching the cadence of Doja’s verse and treating the feature as a regular collaboration.

She also recalled enjoying the video shoot.

“That song was hella natural,” Rico said.

They had performed “Tia Tamera” together at Coachella in 2019, just months after the song came out. Doja brought Rico back for the track during her own Coachella set in 2022. Rico told Glamour that she had watched Doja cross over and was thrilled to get the invitation.

“Doja has features with the coolest people ever and she chose me. I felt very, very special,” Rico said.

The Forum reunion is set to reach viewers next week. Doja’s “Amazon Music Live” performance is scheduled for October 29 after “Thursday Night Football” on Amazon Music, Twitch and Prime Video.

Her episode will close the concert series’ fifth season, which runs four episodes.

item.title: Cardi B Picks Local Shops For Grow-Good’s Retail Debut
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Cardi B brought Grow-Good to two New York beauty supply shops, with four more stores planned in other cities for October 23.
item.content:encoded:
Cardi B brought Grow-Good to two New York beauty supply shops earlier this week after choosing local shops for her launch, not a big chain. Four more stores will join them on October 23.

The first stops were Beautify Beauty Supply in Harlem and Solea in the Bronx, and the next four shops are in Atlanta, Chicago, Houston and Los Angeles.

Cardi has known Beautify owner Tina Hassan for about 10 years. She values shop owners who will give her a straight answer about what they sell.

“If I ask them if they like a product, they’ll be honest with you if they don’t love it,” she told BoF.

Grow-Good is a joint venture between Cardi and fashion retailer Revolve. In its May earnings remarks, Revolve said the brand held a presale in March, then formally launched in April.

The company paired its business and marketing skills with Cardi’s reach beyond its usual shoppers. The teams promoted Grow-Good on social media, on her North American tour and at Revolve Festival.

Her interest in haircare came before the brand. Cardi spent years showing fans how she cared for her natural hair and sharing at-home treatments. She said the idea for her own line came from seeing others try her homemade mask.

She also used the April launch to question what people meant by “good hair.”

Growing up, she had heard that praise aimed at other people’s hair. Her own was left out of the conversation. She described the name as a change in focus: how people could grow their hair.

“So I want people to know that we’re growing our hair good,” Cardi said then.

Grow-Good now sells six products: two shampoos, two conditioners, a mask and a serum. Wash Cycle shampoo and Soft Serve conditioner come in two versions each.

The brand markets the added “+” versions for hair that needs more moisture. Prices on its site run from $14.99 to $19.99. The Get Rich mask costs the most; Everything Serum falls between it and the shampoos.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Damon Dash’s Nemesis Lawyer Chris Brown Won Bid For Life Rights With Film Company
item.dc:creator: Grouchy Greg Watkins (@GrouchyGreg)
item.description: Damon Dash's longtime legal rival Christopher Brown identified himself as a bidder in the bankruptcy sale involving his life story.
item.content:encoded:
Damon Dash spent years fighting attorney Christopher Brown in court, and now, in a shocking turn of events, Brown joined Everlasting Films in its $550,000 bid to win the mogul’s life-story rights and related intellectual property

Brown’s role became clear in an October 23 filing in Dash’s Florida bankruptcy case. The lawyer, who won his own defamation judgment against Dash and represented others who beat him in court, joined the notice naming the auction’s successful and backup bidders.

“Chris Brown, participating bidder with Everlasting, joins in the Notice of Successful Bidder and Back-Up Bidder,” the filing stated.

Brown had already pushed to sell Dash’s life rights. In August, AllHipHop reported that the trustee sought to sell Dash’s name, image and personal story, with Everlasting Films making the opening offer.

Brown’s latest filing confirmed him as a bidder.

The move put Brown on the other side of a fight Dash cited when explaining why he sought bankruptcy protection. During his September 16, 2025 appearance on “The Breakfast Club,” Damon Dash said the lawyer’s collection efforts had disrupted deals involving his family office.

“I filed because you know that guy Chris Brown has been suing me,” Dash said.

Their feud had become personal long before the bankruptcy.

A November 2019 deposition ended with police being called after Dash’s clash with Brown. Judge Robert Lehrburger later ordered Dash to pay $2,744.92 for the failed session.

Brown also sought to restrict Dash’s public attacks, arguing that his social media posts could affect potential jurors. In January 2020, Judge Lehrburger declined to rule on the gag-order request, telling the plaintiffs to file a motion with factual and legal support if they wanted to pursue it.

Brown’s own defamation case grew out of Dash’s public comments about him.

A Los Angeles federal jury found for the attorney on his defamation claim in December 2022. The judgment awarded Brown $50,000 against Damon Dash and another $50,000 against Dash’s company, Poppington, plus interest.

Author Edwyna Brooks won $300,000 in 2020 over Dash’s unauthorized sale and promotion of “Mafietta,” the film based on her books. Brown represented Brooks, and a federal appeals court upheld her award in July 2021.

Damon Dash had argued that he co-owned the film. The appeals court rejected that position, upholding the finding that Brooks hired him to provide services rather than share ownership.

Brown also represented filmmaker Josh Webber and Muddy Water Pictures in their “Dear Frank” dispute with Dash and Poppington.

After a trial over copyright infringement and defamation, the court entered an amended judgment in June 2022 for $705,400. Another $117,884.71 in attorney’s fees followed that September.

Webber also won a separate $4 million defamation judgment against Dash.

Collecting those awards became a fight in its own right.

A June 2025 court order said Webber and Muddy Water had received no proceeds from the auction of Dash’s Roc-A-Fella stake and that their judgment remained unpaid at that point.

Brown had made his approach to collecting from Dash clear years earlier. After Brooks won her case, he told AllHipHop, “We want every penny and I mean every penny.”

item.title: Ric Flair Hospitalized In Tampa After Restaurant Fall
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Ric Flair was hospitalized after a fall outside a Tampa restaurant, hours after announcing a blood clot had limited his travel.
item.content:encoded:
Ric Flair was taken to a hospital after a fall outside a Tampa restaurant on Friday, October 23, hours after he told fans a blood clot had forced him to cancel a Seattle appearance.

The wrestling star, whose friendship with Offset brought him into the “Ric Flair Drip” video and onto late-night television, suffered cuts to his head and eye, according to TMZ Sports.

Sources with direct knowledge told the outlet that Flair had been at Wagamama that morning. He left his phone and drink at the bar, walked across the street and fell while outside. Emergency workers attended to him before an ambulance took him to the hospital, the report said.

Earlier Friday, Flair shared a health update with fans explaining why he couldn’t make his planned Washington State Horror Con appearance. He said doctors had restricted his travel to three or four hours because of a blood clot in his leg.

The trip to Seattle exceeded that limit. He apologized to the organizers and fans who had planned to see him there.

Flair also said he was scheduled for a procedure to strip the affected vein. He said his doctors expected the treatment would let him resume longer trips.

“I Have To Put My Health And Recovery First,” Flair wrote in the statement, which preceded the reported fall.

Flair’s reach has long extended beyond wrestling, with Offset turning his name into a rap hit. “Ric Flair Drip,” made with Metro Boomin, appeared on the pair’s 2017 joint project with 21 Savage, “Without Warning.”

Flair appeared in the song’s video and later joined Offset and Metro Boomin on “The Tonight Show” in April 2018. The performance brought Flair and Offset into a wrestling ring on the late-night set, with The Roots also involved.

Offset carried that bond into WWE the following year. Wearing a pink Ric Flair robe, he introduced Charlotte Flair on “SmackDown” in Atlanta before her match against Sasha Banks.

The elder Flair built that following over decades in the ring. WWE inducted him into its Hall of Fame in 2008, then honored him again in 2012 as part of The Four Horsemen.

item.title: Clavicular Pleads Not Guilty As Judge Bars Posts About Accuser
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Clavicular entered a not-guilty plea as a judge set bail, limited contact with his accuser and scheduled another hearing.
item.content:encoded:
Clavicular pleaded not guilty to a rape charge on October 22, and a Massachusetts judge set $10,000 bail and barred posts about his accuser.

The September case report also described a separate charge of providing alcohol to a minor.

The accuser told police Clavicular had paid her to appear in videos and gave her alcohol during a May 2025 visit to his family’s Chatham home. She says he sexually assaulted her there when she was 17.

His lawyers say the encounter was consensual. Attorney David Meier said the two had a professional and personal relationship for almost a year, according to the Associated Press. Clavicular did not answer reporters’ questions as he left the courthouse.

His lawyer entered the plea in Orleans District Court. Judge John Julian ordered the 20-year-old to surrender his passport and avoid his accuser, ABC News reported.

“If you commit a new offense, whether it be state or federal, I could hold you without bail for up to 90 days,” Julian told Clavicular.

The hearing follows the charges AllHipHop reported in September. At that stage, attorney Steve Kramer denied the allegations and said he would fight them in court.

Clavicular built his online following around “looksmaxxing,” a pursuit of physical attractiveness that can include cosmetic surgery, steroids and other extreme measures.

The civil suit also alleges he injected her with a fat-dissolving substance during a livestream without consent.

A related Florida civil lawsuit is separate from the criminal case. ABC reported that the accuser removed sexual-assault allegations from that suit earlier this month. Her lawyers said she did not want the civil case to interfere with the prosecution. That change did not end the criminal charge.

The case carries stakes beyond Clavicular’s online reputation. The September report noted that a rape conviction in Massachusetts can bring up to 20 years in prison.

Clavicular is due back in court November 24 for a probable-cause hearing.
